accepted_claims.claim: There exists an absolute C>0 and infinitely many positive integers n with omega(n-k)<=Omega(n-k)<=C log k for every integer 2<=k<n.
There exists one fixed epsilon>0 and infinitely many N such that m+epsilon*Omega(m)<=N for every positive integer m<N, hence the same with distinct omega.
accepted_claims.proof: N=n-1, epsilon=1/(C log 2); j=N-m, k=j+1, log(j+1)<=j log 2.

not_established: Coefficient-one omega barrier at every positive m<N for infinitely many N.
Any claim that all broad-parameter lemmas or all printed proof steps of the source are correct.
terminal_window: Coefficient one remains controlled only beyond a fixed cutoff; every smaller shift, including shift 1, remains a separate simultaneous obligation.
corrections: Replace false complex-kernel L1 equality by exact local-factor separation and absolutely summed nonnegative-translation operators.
Use fixed moment orders, avoiding the source parameter mismatch.
Bound all higher-power CRT errors with a fixed A=100 budget and Q^s<=x^.02.
Keep signed CRT main terms but bound interval-count errors by absolute coefficient sums.
